## Exploring the KM-GBF model database

This is a walk through of how to explore the KM-GBF model database at xxxx.

## Loading in the database

You can load the database in with the function *LoadDatabaseinR*

```{r}
targets::tar_source("../R")
model_database <- LoadDatabaseInR(dataset_path = "../input/Merged_Dataset_KMGBF_16Oct25.xlsx")


```

## What variables can we visualize?

Not all questions lend themselves easily to visualisations so when exploring the database it is good to know which columns contain information that we can plot.

```{r}

visual_columns <- .ColumnsWithAttributes(model_database)

head(visual_columns)

visual_columns
```

It is through these columns that we can go and explore the database

## Metadata figures

```{r}

Realm <- ResponseCount(database = model_database,
              response = visual_columns[3], radial = TRUE)


ggplot2::ggsave(Realm,filename = "../outputs/figures/metadata/realm.png",  device = "png", width = 30.5, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 400)

Drivers <- ResponseCount(database = model_database,
              response = visual_columns[7], radial = TRUE)


ggplot2::ggsave(Drivers,filename = "../outputs/figures/metadata/drivers.png",  device = "png", width = 30.5, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 400)


Domain <- ResponseCount(database = model_database,
              response = visual_columns[1], radial = TRUE)


ggplot2::ggsave(Domain,filename = "../outputs/figures/metadata/domain.png",  device = "png", width = 30.5, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 400)


NFF <- ResponseCount(database = model_database,
              response = visual_columns[39], radial = TRUE)


ggplot2::ggsave(NFF,filename = "../outputs/figures/metadata/NFF.png",  device = "png", width = 30.5, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 400)


Goals <- ResponseCount(database = model_database,
              response = visual_columns[29], radial = TRUE)


ggplot2::ggsave(Goals,filename = "../outputs/figures/metadata/kmgbf_goals.png",  device = "png", width = 30.5, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 400)


Targets <- ResponseCount(database = model_database,
              response = visual_columns[31], radial = TRUE)


ggplot2::ggsave(Targets,filename = "../outputs/figures/metadata/kmgbf_targets.png",  device = "png", width = 30.5, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 400)

```
